subject: FinPay — brief service interruption: streaming microbursts and interim workarounds
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Li <alex.li@finpay.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 16:20:00 -0700
Subject: FinPay — brief service interruption: streaming microbursts and interim workarounds

Alex —

I wanted to flag that earlier today (around 16:05–16:18 PDT) our telemetry detected short "microburst" latency events affecting streaming responses for requests routed to the us-west-2 streaming pool used by your account. The symptom you experienced (brief pauses of 2–6s during live streamed assistant responses, then recovery) matches those spikes.

Immediate notes: we have captured full traces and a kernel-level snapshot for the affected shard and attached the diagnostic bundle to this thread (diagnostic_logs_20270519.zip). We are investigating root cause — preliminary signs point to a short-lived preemption/IO jitter event on a small subset of nodes during a maintenance window that coincided with traffic microbursts.

Short-term mitigation we can apply on our side today (no code changes on your end):
- Route your streaming traffic to the standby pool for ~2h to avoid the affected machines (we can toggle transparently).
- Temporarily enable more aggressive prefix caching for your top 5 session templates to reduce per-request work.
- If you prefer client-side mitigations, recommended safe fallbacks are below.

We’ll keep you updated as we triage. If you can share a few example request IDs (or we can map them from the attached traces) that will help speed root-cause. Sorry for the disruption — we know these pauses are disruptive for live UX.

—Rafael
Rafael Mendes

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FinPay — brief service interruption: streaming microbursts and interim workarounds

Thanks Rafael — quick technical update that I'll share with FinPay so you have concrete workarounds while we remediate: 

Summary of what we see from the traces (customer-facing summary):
- Several nodes in the us-west-2 streaming pool recorded brief kernel-level scheduling latency (~30–80ms bursts stacking) at the same time as a maintenance IO window. That caused batching and token emission to stall briefly for affected sessions.

Customer-facing mitigations (short term, low-friction):
1) Switch to polite polling for critical flows: instead of streaming, poll for newly generated tokens every 300–500ms. Polling avoids relying on an uninterrupted TCP streaming channel and will give a more consistent UX during microbursts.
2) Reduce max_tokens and split long responses: cap max_tokens to 350 and emit multiple shorter responses (2–3 segments) so individual emissions are less affected by a single stall.
3) Client-side retry/backoff for stalled streams: detect >2s no-token gap and automatically retry the request (idempotent safety recommended).

Planned actions from our side:
- We'll route your traffic to the standby pool for the next 3 hours and monitor.
- Run a control patch to avoid scheduling proximity to maintenance windows on the streaming fleet.

I'll mark this as high priority and update with a postmortem within 48 hours. Rafael — if FinPay prefers us to execute the routing change now, I can trigger it.

—Monica
Monica Patel
Head of Incident Response, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai

Thanks Rafael and Monica — appreciate the quick flag. Two quick questions: 

1) Can you confirm whether routing to the standby pool will cause any config changes on our side (we need to notify our on-call)?
2) If we switch to polling for critical payment validation flows, can you suggest a compact polling cadence that balances latency and cost?

Also we're seeing this mostly on our nightly peak (17:45–18:00 PDT) — if the routing change will happen immediately that should cover it. Regarding credits, Finance will likely ask for a brief incident credit for the time impacted; who should I loop in to start that conversation?

—Alex

FinPay

Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FinPay — brief service interruption: streaming microbursts and interim workarounds

Alex —

Answers inline: 
1) Routing change scope: No config changes needed on your side. This is a server-side routing adjustment; we'll transparently send your streaming sessions to the standby pool for the next 3 hours and then validate. I will notify you when we flip it and when we flip back.

2) Polling cadence recommendation: 300–500ms polling is a good balance for interactive payment validations. For the highest-sensitivity flows (card-present confirmations) you can poll at 300ms for the first 2s, then back off to 600ms. This reduces the perceived latency while limiting extra tokens.

Credit/finance: I’ve looped in Ben Carter (CC) from Customer Success to start a credit review and Laura Bennett (CC) who handles billing adjustments for enterprise accounts. Ben — can you confirm the standard incident credit process and a rough timeline for FinPay?

Next steps from Redwood:
- [Immediate] Route to standby pool (in progress).
- [Immediate] Increase prefix caching for FinPay session templates.
- [Within 48h] Full postmortem with RCA and mitigation plan.

We’ll follow up with a formal postmortem doc and a proposed SLA adjustment if desired. Sorry again for the friction — we’ll keep this top priority.

—Rafael
Rafael Mendes
